items.title: Jimmy Wormworth interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: the piano player that works with Charles Davis, which is who I work with now

ctx.x: And they believe in themselves a lot. They have a lot of confidence. Elvin. Now who’s more confident than Elvin? Most of the drummers I know who I admire, they tend to have some swagger. Max definitely had swagger. And I think I have a short attention span. I tend to be intensely interested for a minute then all of a sudden I get distracted. I

think I have ADD. My colleague and friend Tardo Hammer, the piano player that works with Charles Davis, which is who I work with now, he said, “No I don’t think you have ADD.” I said I think I do. I can’t concentrate.
I don’t know, you just move from one drum to the next you know. You’ve got enough drums there to take care of it I think.
